title: SecID Registry Namespace
description: Validates SecID registry namespace JSON files. Each file describes one namespace (organization) within a single SecID type, including identity, resolution URLs, and pattern trees for matching subpath identifiers.

schema_version.description: JSON schema version for this file.

namespace.description: Organization identifier — domain name, optionally with /path segments (e.g., 'mitre.org', 'github.com/advisories').

type.description: SecID type this namespace belongs to.

status.description: Registry entry status reflecting documentation completeness and review state.

status_notes.description: Optional context about status (blockers, gaps, guidance for contributors).

notes.description: Free-form context for AI and human readers. Markdown allowed.

alias_of.description: If present, this is an alias stub — namespace redirects to the target value. No sources needed.

wikipedia.description: Wikipedia article URLs for direct access.

checked.description: Date someone last verified the entry is still accurate (YYYY-MM-DD).

updated.description: Date the entry last materially changed (YYYY-MM-DD).

urls.description: Top-level URLs for the organization (website, docs, API, etc.).

match_nodes.description: Pattern tree for matching SecID name/subpath components. Each node matches a portion of the SecID string and optionally has children for deeper matching.

tags.description: Optional filterable metadata (country, sector, etc.) for this namespace as a whole. Same shape as a match_node's data.tags (see MatchNode). Resolution is per-level, not merged: a query for the namespace gets these tags; a query for a specific source/subpath gets that node's own data.tags if present, otherwise falls back to these. Keys are open/uncontrolled for now — see docs/reference/REGISTRY-JSON-FORMAT.md.

UrlObject.description: A URL with type classification and optional metadata.

type.description: URL category: website, docs, api, bulk_data, lookup, security, security_txt, paper, github, search, secid_api, secid_mcp, etc.

note.description: Human/AI-readable context explaining what this URL is for.

format.description: Expected content format: html, json, pdf, xml, csv, zip.

checked.description: Date this URL was last verified (YYYY-MM-DD).

updated.description: Date this URL entry last changed (YYYY-MM-DD).

MatchNode.description: A pattern tree node. Matches a portion of the SecID string (name, version, subpath, or item_version) via regex patterns. Returns data when matched and optionally recurses into children for the next portion.

patterns.description: One or more regex patterns (OR alternatives). All share the same children and data. Use (?i) prefix for case-insensitive matching.

description.description: Human/AI-readable description of what this node matches.

weight.description: Match quality/preference. 0-200, higher is more preferred. Returned with results so consumers can sort.

data.description: Result data returned when this node matches. Contents vary by tree depth and SecID type — name-level nodes have source metadata, subpath-level nodes have resolution URLs. Open-ended: different types use different fields.

children.description: Child nodes for matching the next portion of the SecID string. Recursive structure.

Tags.description: Filterable metadata: a dict of key -> array of string values (always an array, even for a single value). Keys are open/uncontrolled for now (e.g. 'country' with ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes plus 'EU'/'INTL', 'sector'). Not validated beyond shape — see docs/reference/REGISTRY-JSON-FORMAT.md for the current starter conventions. Can appear at the namespace's top-level 'tags' field or inside any match_node's 'data.tags' field (the latter is not schema-enforced since MatchNode.data is open-ended, but should follow this same shape).

VersionAlias.description: An alternate label for the version entry this object is nested under. Publishers routinely label one release two ways: CSA stamps the AICM workbook 1.1.0 while branding the same release 'v1.1' on its download page, and does the reverse for CCM where 4.1 is canonical and 4.1.0 is the variant. Nesting encodes the target, so there is no pointer to dangle. IMPORTANT: this object is metadata only. Matching is done by the pattern tree — the alias label must also appear as an OR-pattern on the corresponding version node, or it will never resolve. scripts/validate-version-aliases.py enforces that binding.

label.description: The alias exactly as the publisher writes it. Never normalized — no case folding, no 'v' stripping, no semver inference. Must not equal a real version string in the same source.

on_match.description: What a resolver does when this label matches. 'resolve' returns full data inline with status 'found' and version_matched_alias set — for co-equal publisher labels. 'redirect' returns empty results with status 'corrected' and the canonical SecID in the message — for labels that should be retired. Reserved and deliberately unimplemented: 'track' (a moving pointer to the latest matching version). Resolvers must ignore alias entries whose on_match they do not recognize, so reserved values can ship later without breaking deployed resolvers.

note.description: Where this label appears, or why it exists.

VersionEntry.description: One known version of a source, in a match_node's data.versions_available array. Each entry must correspond to a version-level node in that source's pattern tree whose patterns[0] is the canonical version string; the validator enforces this both ways. Not schema-enforced here, because versions_available lives inside match_nodes[].data and data is additionalProperties:true — see scripts/validate-version-aliases.py.

version.description: The canonical version string, exactly as the artifact identifies itself. Where a publisher's download page and the artifact disagree, the artifact wins and the page's label becomes an alias.

release_date.description: ISO date, or null if researched and unknown.

note.description: What a consumer needs to know about this specific version — item counts, mapping changes, ID-stability warnings, sourcing caveats.

aliases.description: Alternate labels for this version. Each must also appear as an OR-pattern on the corresponding version node in the tree.
